title: tests/harness.py lifecycle helpers skip HA's on_unload processing: 1 shutdown per unload (HA 2), 4 leaks per NotReady (HA 0)
claim: The suite's entry-manager instrument diverges from Home Assistant's ConfigEntry in two seams of one mechanism (_async_process_on_unload): ha_unload_entry calls each async_on_unload callback FIFO and drops a returned coroutine, so HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown runs once per unload where HA runs it twice (1 RuntimeWarning per unload; store saves 3 vs 4 per unload); and ha_setup_entry runs no unload callback when async_setup_entry raises ConfigEntryNotReady, so each failed attempt leaves 4 live registrations reaching its coordinator and the coordinator alive (3 of 3 after 3 failures), where HA's order leaves 0 and 0.
mechanism: homeassistant ConfigEntry._async_process_on_unload: `while self._on_unload: if job := self._on_unload.pop()(): self.async_create_task(hass, job)` then awaits the tasks; the stub DataUpdateCoordinator registers `config_entry.async_on_unload(self.async_shutdown)` as upstream does; tests/harness.py:ha_unload_entry runs `callback()` and drops the result. Every suite test unloading through it therefore never runs the second HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown (pump_arbiter.release -> _persist a second time, legionella release, forget_held) that a real unload runs. On ConfigEntryNotReady HA's ConfigEntry.async_setup also awaits _async_process_on_unload (the coordinator's own _release_registrations and the base-class async_shutdown), which tests/harness.py:ha_setup_entry never runs: production's #236 cleanup is therefore unobservable through the suite's helper, and a test that counts registrations after a NotReady sees leaks HA would not have.

evidence.unit: async_shutdown runs per unload (harness instrument; HA order gives 2)
evidence.machine: box B4 container, linux x86_64, Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: part B of m4_race.py and other finder seats on the box; counts, contention-immune; thread_factor after subtracting executor-thread CPU

perturbation.change: one-line instrument repair in ha_unload_entry: `if inspect.isawaitable(r := callback()): await r` (arm --unload harness_awaiting)

metric_definition: async_shutdown entries per unload over 3 unloads of one lifecycle (1 vs 2); and live registrations reaching a failed attempt's coordinator after 3 NotReady setups (12 vs 0).
phenomenon_property: The suite's entry-manager helpers must run what Home Assistant's ConfigEntry runs at unload and at a failed setup: every async_on_unload callback, popped last-first, a returned awaitable awaited.

null_control.value: 2 shutdowns per unload, 0 dropped coroutines, 12 saves; 0 failed-attempt leaks, 0 alive
null_control.note: HA's order (rl.ha_unload_faithful / process_on_unload). The NotReady seam: --setup harness gives failed_attempt_leaks=12 (running_signal.py:112, :194, away.py:260, coordinator.py:8746 x3), failed_attempts_alive=3.

proposed_fix_scope: tests/harness.py: ha_unload_entry pops LIFO and awaits a returned awaitable; ha_setup_entry runs the same processing when async_setup_entry raises ConfigEntryNotReady (as rl.ha_unload_faithful / m1_notready.process_on_unload do). Production impact: none found (HA's order leaks nothing); one redundant pump_duty save per unload.
